stem: Which statement best describes an **embedded system**?

options.content: A microprocessor-based system with a dedicated function inside a larger device
options.rationale: Correct: the dedicated function inside a larger device is the key idea.

options.content: A computer that can run any program the user chooses to install on it
options.rationale: That describes a general-purpose computer such as a PC or laptop.

options.content: A program that is copied into RAM when the computer starts up
options.rationale: An embedded system is hardware plus software, not just a program.

options.content: A very large computer that serves many users over a network at once
options.rationale: That describes a server or mainframe.

explanation: An embedded system is built around a microprocessor and performs a dedicated function as part of a larger device.

stem: Which device is a **general-purpose** computer rather than an embedded system?

options.content: A laptop
options.rationale: Correct: a laptop runs many different programs for many tasks.

options.content: The controller in a microwave oven
options.rationale: It only controls the microwave: an embedded system.

options.content: An anti-lock braking system in a car
options.rationale: It has one dedicated job: an embedded system.

options.content: The controller of an electric gate
options.rationale: It only opens and closes the gate: an embedded system.

explanation: PCs and laptops are general-purpose; appliances, car systems and gate controllers contain embedded systems.

stem: Where is the program that controls a washing machine's embedded system usually stored?

options.content: In RAM, loaded from a hard disk each time
options.rationale: Washing machines have no hard disk; RAM is volatile.

options.content: On a DVD inserted by the user
options.rationale: The user does not load the program.

options.content: In ROM or flash memory, as firmware
options.rationale: Correct: the fixed program must be kept when the power is off.

options.content: In cloud storage, downloaded for every wash
options.rationale: The machine must work without an internet connection.

explanation: Embedded systems run firmware held in non-volatile memory (ROM or flash), so it is there every time the device is switched on.

stem: Which is a **characteristic** of most embedded systems?

options.content: A full keyboard and a large screen
options.rationale: Most have a simple interface or none at all.

options.content: Low power consumption
options.rationale: Correct: many run on batteries or are switched on all the time.

options.content: The user can install any application
options.rationale: The firmware is fixed by the manufacturer.

options.content: Large size and high cost
options.rationale: They are small and cheap to mass-produce.

explanation: Embedded systems are small, cheap, low-power and have a dedicated function.

stem: Which part of a car is **most likely** to be controlled by an embedded system?

options.content: The seat fabric
options.rationale: Fabric has no electronics.

options.content: The fuel tank
options.rationale: The tank itself stores fuel; it does not process data.

options.content: The airbag system
options.rationale: Correct: it monitors sensors and fires the airbag in real time.

options.content: The windscreen glass
options.rationale: Glass has no processor.

explanation: Car embedded systems include engine management, anti-lock brakes, airbags and navigation.

stem: Why must the embedded system that controls a car's anti-lock brakes respond in **real time**?

options.content: It must save every reading to secondary storage before acting on it
options.rationale: Saving first would delay the response.

options.content: It must react to wheel sensor readings immediately, or the car could skid
options.rationale: Correct: a delayed response would be dangerous.

options.content: It must wait for the driver to confirm each action on a screen
options.rationale: The system acts automatically, without the driver.

options.content: It must download new firmware before every journey
options.rationale: Firmware is fixed; it is not downloaded each journey.

explanation: Real-time systems respond to inputs immediately; for brakes and airbags any delay could cause an accident.
hints: Think about what an airbag or a brake system must do the moment something happens.

stem: Which is a **drawback** of an embedded system that is connected to the internet so it can be controlled by a phone app?

options.content: It can be switched on remotely before the owner arrives home
options.rationale: That is a benefit of remote control.

options.content: It uses very little electrical power
options.rationale: Low power is a benefit.

options.content: It is cheap to manufacture in large numbers
options.rationale: Low cost is a benefit.

options.content: It could be hacked and controlled by an unauthorised person
options.rationale: Correct: connected devices need to be kept secure.

explanation: Remote control is convenient, but an insecure connected device can be hacked.
hints: Which is a drawback, not a benefit?

stem: Thandeka says a smart television with a fixed set of built-in features is an embedded system, but her desktop PC is not. Which reason supports her view?

options.content: The television has a larger screen and better speakers than the desktop PC
options.rationale: Screen size does not decide whether a system is embedded.

options.content: The television uses electricity, but the PC uses a battery
options.rationale: Both use mains electricity; power source is not the test.

options.content: The PC has no microprocessor, so it cannot be embedded
options.rationale: A PC does have a microprocessor; it is general-purpose.

options.content: The television's processor performs dedicated functions within a larger device
options.rationale: Correct: the dedicated function within a larger device is what makes it embedded.

explanation: An embedded system performs dedicated functions inside a larger device; a desktop PC runs any software the user installs.
hints: Ask whether the device has one dedicated function and whether the user can install other programs.

stem: An automatic street light that switches on at dusk is controlled by an embedded system.
explanation: True. It has one dedicated function: reading a light sensor and switching the lamp.

stem: The owner of a microwave oven can normally install a new word-processing program on its embedded system.
explanation: False. Embedded systems run fixed firmware; the user cannot install general applications.

stem: Match each embedded system to its dedicated function.

right.content: Controls fuel and ignition from sensor readings
Keeps the inside at a set temperature
Checks motion sensors and sounds a siren
Accepts payment and releases the chosen item

explanation: Each embedded system has one dedicated function inside a larger device.

payload.template: An embedded system performs a {{blank:a}} function as part of a larger device. Its program, called {{blank:b}}, is stored in non-volatile memory. A PC or laptop is a {{blank:c}} computer because it runs many different programs.

stem: Give the term for a computer, such as a PC or laptop, that can perform many different tasks by running different programs.
explanation: A general-purpose computer runs many different programs; an embedded system has a dedicated function.

stem: State **three** characteristics of an embedded system. [3]

points.description: Performs a dedicated function / is part of a larger device
Small / cheap to mass-produce / low power consumption
Fixed program (firmware) in ROM or flash / responds in real time / simple or no user interface

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It has a dedicated function within a larger device; it is small and uses little power; it runs fixed firmware stored in ROM.

explanation: Credit one point from each line.
hints: Give three different features, not three examples.

stem: A security company in Bulawayo fits houses with alarms controlled by embedded systems that the owner can arm from a phone app. Give **two** benefits and **two** drawbacks of using an internet-connected embedded system in the alarm. [4]

points.description: Benefit: owner can arm/disarm or check the alarm remotely (from anywhere)
Benefit: small, low power, reliable, responds immediately to sensors / low cost
Drawback: could be hacked so a criminal could disarm it
Drawback: needs an internet connection to be controlled remotely / difficult to upgrade / whole unit replaced if it fails

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The owner can arm it from anywhere, and the embedded system uses little power and responds at once to the sensors. However, a hacker could take control and disarm it, and remote control fails if the internet connection is lost.

explanation: Balance remote control and reliability against security and dependence on the connection.
hints: Link each point to the alarm.

stem: A bakery in Mutare buys an oven controlled by an embedded system. The baker chooses a programme on a keypad; the oven heats to the right temperature and switches off when the time is up.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which component would the embedded system use to measure the oven's temperature?

options.content: An actuator
options.rationale: An actuator causes movement or switches something; it does not measure.

options.content: A temperature sensor
options.rationale: Correct: it sends readings to the processor.

options.content: A speaker
options.rationale: A speaker outputs sound.

options.content: A barcode scanner
options.rationale: It reads barcodes, not temperature.

parts.explanation: The sensor measures; the processor decides; the heater (or a relay) is switched.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe how the embedded system keeps the oven at the chosen temperature.

points.description: The temperature sensor sends readings to the microprocessor
The microprocessor compares each reading with the stored/chosen temperature
If it is too low the heater is switched on, if too high it is switched off; this repeats continuously

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The sensor sends the temperature to the microprocessor, which compares it with the chosen value. If it is too low the heater is switched on, and if it is too high it is switched off; this repeats continuously until the time is up.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why the oven uses an embedded system rather than a general-purpose computer.

points.description: It only needs to perform one dedicated function (controlling the oven)
An embedded system is smaller / cheaper / uses less power / more reliable than a PC

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The oven only has one dedicated job, so a small, cheap, low-power embedded system is enough; a PC would cost more and use more power for no benefit.

explanation: Sensor → microprocessor compares → heater switched; embedded because of the dedicated function, size and cost.
hints: Compare with a PC: one job versus many.

stem: Tendai lists some devices in his home: a desktop computer, a digital alarm clock, an air conditioner, a laptop, a tablet computer and an electric gate opener.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Select the **three** devices that contain embedded systems.

options.content: Electric gate opener
options.rationale: Correct: opens and closes the gate.

options.content: Digital alarm clock
options.rationale: Correct: dedicated function.

options.content: Desktop computer
options.rationale: General-purpose.

options.content: Tablet computer
options.rationale: General-purpose: the user installs and runs many apps.

options.content: Air conditioner
options.rationale: Correct: controls temperature and the fan.

options.content: Laptop
options.rationale: General-purpose.

parts.explanation: The clock, air conditioner and gate opener each have a dedicated function.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Give **two** differences between an embedded system and a general-purpose computer.

points.description: Embedded: one dedicated function; general-purpose: many tasks / runs many programs
Embedded: fixed firmware the user cannot change / simple interface / smaller, cheaper, lower power

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An embedded system does one dedicated job, while a PC runs many programs. The embedded system's firmware is fixed, but a PC user can install new software.

explanation: Clock, air conditioner and gate opener are embedded; the desktop and laptop are general-purpose.
hints: Dedicated function inside a larger device = embedded.
